endpoint.text: The hydrolysis degree (DH) and soluble peptides of HAHp were (18.12 ± 0.39)% and (81.78 ± 0.04)%, respectively, measured by the method described in Song et al. [31].
The separation was performed using a linear gradient from 15% to 45% B in 40 min at a flow rate of 2.0 mL/min, measured at 215 nm.

reported_results.text: The antibacterial activity of cationic peptides can be modulated through modification of net charge or the ratio of hydrophobicity [21,22].
HAHp-catoinic1 had intermediate net charges (+2) and hydrophobicity ratio (42%).
In contrast, HAHp-cationic3 had the highest hydrophobic ratio (50%) and the lowest cationic charges (+1).
HAHp-catoinic2 possessed the highest cationic charges (+3), whereas its hydrophobic ratio (21%) was the lowest among the five cationic peptides.
Our results of the prediction of peptide secondary structure shown in Table 2 are similar to that study, and concordant with the antibacterial activity exhibited by fraction HAHp2-3-I. 2.4.

The separated peaks were analyzed by a LTQ-Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo, Waltham, MA, USA) under ESI positive ionization mode (+2.5 Kv ionspray voltage, 200 °C capillary temperature), scanning from a mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) of 400–1,800.

The hydrolysis degree (DH) and soluble peptides of HAHp were (18.12 ± 0.39)% and (81.78 ± 0.04)%, respectively, measured by the method described in Song et al. [31].

In contrast, HAHp-cationic3 had the highest hydrophobic ratio (50%) and the lowest cationic charges (+1).
HAHp-catoinic2 possessed the highest cationic charges (+3), whereas its hydrophobic ratio (21%) was the lowest among the five cationic peptides.
Our results of the prediction of peptide secondary structure shown in Table 2 are similar to that study, and concordant with the antibacterial activity exhibited by fraction HAHp2-3-I. 2.4.

The separated peaks were analyzed by a LTQ-Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo, Waltham, MA, USA) under ESI positive ionization mode (+2.5 Kv ionspray voltage, 200 °C capillary temperature), scanning from a mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) of 400–1,800.
